questions.question_text: The use of lithium was first initiated by:

options.text: Pritchard
Kraepelin
Cade
Kahlbaum
Henderson

questions.explanation: Kraepelin developed the concept of dementia praecox; Kahlbaum described catatonia.

questions.question_text: Hypomania is a disorder characterized by all of the following, except:

options.text: Persistent elevation of mood
Decreased need for sleep
Increased sexual energy
Overfamiliarity
Severe disruption of work and symptoms that lead to social rejection

correct_answer.text: Severe disruption of work and symptoms that lead to social rejection

correct_answers.text: Severe disruption of work and symptoms that lead to social rejection

questions.explanation: When severe disruption of work and symptoms that lead to social rejection occur, the illness is classified as mania.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about classification of affective disorders in ICD-10, except:

options.text: It allows for the diagnosis of single first episodes of hypomania without the overall diagnosis of bipolar disorder
It requires a single episode of mania with psychotic symptoms to be classified as bipolar disease
Two or more episodes of hypomania or mania without depressive episodes should be classified as bipolar disorder
To make a diagnosis of mania, the mood change must be prominent and sustained for at least 1 week, unless it is severe enough to require hospital admission

In a second episode of affective disorder, if manic and depressive symptoms are prominent most of the time during a 2-week period, a diagnosis of bipolardisorder, with currentepisodemixed, could be made

correct_answer.text: It requires a single episode of mania with psychotic symptoms to be classified as bipolar disease

correct_answers.text: It requires a single episode of mania with psychotic symptoms to be classified as bipolar disease

questions.explanation: For the diagnosis of bipolar affective disorder, ICD-10 requires two or more episodes of disturbance in a patient's mood or activity level. These could be either one episode of depression and one episode of mania/hypomania, or two episodes of mania/hypomania. A single episode of mania with psychotic symptoms cannot be classified as bipolar disease.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about classification of depressive episode in ICD-10, except:

options.text: A fifth character in the coding may be used to specify the presence or absence of a somatic syndrome in depression
The presence or absence of the somatic syndrome is not specified for severe depressive episode
To make a diagnosis, the depressive episode should last for 2 weeks
To make a diagnosis of severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms, the hallucinations and delusions must be mood congruent
In recurrent depressive disorder, brief episodes of mild hypomanic-type symptoms occur, especially precipitated by antidepressants

correct_answer.text: To make a diagnosis of severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms, the hallucinations and delusions must be mood congruent

correct_answers.text: To make a diagnosis of severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms, the hallucinations and delusions must be mood congruent

questions.explanation: The hallucinations and delusions may or may not be mood congruent.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about depression, except:

options.text: Learned helplessness is described as an important cognitive symptom of depression in ICD-10
Dysthymia is a chronic, less severe depression and ICD-10 and DSM-IV require a duration of at least 2 years to diagnose this condition
Development of depression in dysthymia is known as double depression
Masked depression is more common in the undeveloped world
In seasonal affective disorder, depressive episodes commence in the autumn or winter months and end in the spring or summer

correct_answer.text: Learned helplessness is described as an important cognitive symptom of depression in ICD-10

correct_answers.text: Learned helplessness is described as an important cognitive symptom of depression in ICD-10

questions.explanation: Learned helplessness is the cognitive theory that explains depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Childbirth can cause mania
10% of people with an initial episode of depression develop mania later
Depression is more common in females in all age groups
The average age of onset of bipolar disorder is around the mid-20s
Bipolar disorder is more common in upper social classes

correct_answer.text: Depression is more common in females in all age groups

correct_answers.text: Depression is more common in females in all age groups

questions.explanation: Male first admissions with depression continue to climb until the end of life, overtaking women at the age of 85.

questions.question_text: Which of the following may be more common in depression in old age?

options.text: Hypochondriachal preoccupations
Depressive pseudodementia
Psychomotor retardation or agitation
Behavioural disturbances like shoplifting
All of the above

questions.explanation: Paranoid and delusional ideation, denial of low mood, complaints of loneliness, etc. are common.

questions.question_text: Regarding affective disorders in elderly people, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The Geriatric Depression Scale is helpful in the assessment as it focuses entirely on physical symptoms of depression rather than cognitive symptoms
Depressed patients with ischaemic brain lesions have more vascular risk factors and less family history of mood disorders than those without
Hypo- and hyperthyroidism can present as depression
The age of onset of manic episode is bimodally distributed, with peaks at 37 and 73 years
Late-onset mania cases appear to have less genetic loading than younger-onset cases

correct_answer.text: The Geriatric Depression Scale is helpful in the assessment as it focuses entirely on physical symptoms of depression rather than cognitive symptoms

correct_answers.text: The Geriatric Depression Scale is helpful in the assessment as it focuses entirely on physical symptoms of depression rather than cognitive symptoms

questions.explanation: The Geriatric Depression Scale focuses entirely on cognitive symptoms and is thus helpful.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of rapid cycling bipolar disorder?

options.text: It is characterized by two or more episodes of affective disorders within 12 months
It is more common in men
It responds well to lithium
Concomitant hypothyroidism is common
50% of cases are induced by antidepressants

questions.explanation: It is characterized by four or more episodes in 12 months; it is more common in women; lithium is relatively ineffective; 20% of cases are triggered by antidepressants.

questions.question_text: In DSM-IV:

options.text: The presence of a single episode of hypomania or mania is sufficient to meet the criteria for bipolar affective disorder
Bipolar disorder is separated into bipolar I and bipolar II
The diagnosis of bipolar II is intended to indicate the importance of detecting mild hypomanic episodes
Antidepressant-induced mania/hypomania is not included in the diagnosis of bipolar I or bipolar II
All of the above

questions.explanation: Bipolar I refers to major depression alternating with mania; bipolar II is major depression alternating with hypomania.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding the epidemiology of bipolar and unipolar (major depression)?

options.text: Lifetime risk of bipolar disorder is higher than unipolar disorder
Lifetime risk of an affective illness is higher in first-degree relatives of patients with unipolar illness than in first degree relatives of patients with bipolar disorder
Both bipolar and unipolar disorders occur more commonly in females
Average age of onset is higher in bipolar disorder than unipolar disorder
All of the above

correct_answer.text: Lifetime risk of an affective illness is higher in first-degree relatives of patients with unipolar illness than in first degree relatives of patients with bipolar disorder

correct_answers.text: Lifetime risk of an affective illness is higher in first-degree relatives of patients with unipolar illness than in first degree relatives of patients with bipolar disorder

questions.explanation: The lifetime risk of bipolar disorder (BPD) is 1% and of unipolar disorder (UPD) 10–20%; in first-degree relatives of people with BPD, lifetime risk of BPD is 10% and of UPD 2%; in first-degree relatives of people with UPD, lifetime risk of BPD and UPD is 10–15%; the male:female sex ratio for BPD is 1:1 and UPD 1:2; the average age of onset of BPD is 21 years and UPD 27 years.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is aetiologically linked to mood disorders?

options.text: Chromosomes 4, 12 and 18
Cyclothymic personality
Childhood physical and sexual abuse
Overprotective parental style
All of the above

questions.explanation: In certain families, manic depressive illness has been X-linked to colour blindness and glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency.

questions.question_text: Which of the following includes endocrine causes of depression?

options.text: Cushing's syndrome
Addison's disease
Hypothyroidism
Hyperparathyroidism
All of the above

questions.explanation: 83% of patients with Cushing's syndrome develop affective disorder. Hypoparathyroidism is also associated with depression.

questions.question_text: Suicide:

options.text: Suicide is more common in women
Suicide is more common in people aged less than 45
Suicide rates are highest in winter
Suicide rates fall in times of war and natural calamities
Suicide rates are lowest in social classes I and V

correct_answer.text: Suicide rates fall in times of war and natural calamities

correct_answers.text: Suicide rates fall in times of war and natural calamities

questions.explanation: Suicide is more common in men and people over 45, among those who are single, divorced or widowed, and in social classes I and V. Rates are higher in spring and early summer.

questions.question_text: Regarding psychiatric problems and suicide, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: 90% of people who commit suicide suffer from a psychiatric disorder
90% of psychiatric patients who commit suicide suffer from depression
10% of the mortality in schizophrenia is from suicide
5% of psychiatric patients who commit suicide suffer from schizophrenia
15% of the mortality in alcoholism is from suicide

correct_answer.text: 90% of psychiatric patients who commit suicide suffer from depression

correct_answers.text: 90% of psychiatric patients who commit suicide suffer from depression

questions.explanation: 50% of psychiatric patients who commit suicide suffer from depression.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about deliberate self-harm (DSH), except:

options.text: Following an act of DSH, the risk of committing suicide in the first year is approximately 100 times higher than that in the general population
It is more common in females
It is more common in people below the age of 35 years
The highest rates are in upper social classes
90% of cases involve deliberate self-poisoning

correct_answer.text: The highest rates are in upper social classes

correct_answers.text: The highest rates are in upper social classes

questions.explanation: Deliberate self-harm is more common in lower social classes.

questions.question_text: The Tuckman and Youngman scale for assessment of risk factors for subsequent completion of suicide awards one point to each of the following criteria, except:

options.text: Age above 35
Unemployed
Living alone
Recent medical treatment
Violent attempt

questions.explanation: The scale awards one point to the following criteria in addition to the other choices given in the question: age above 45; male; not married; poor physical health; psychiatric disorder; and previous suicide attempt.

questions.question_text: The term 'neurasthenia' was introduced by:

options.text: Beard
Hecker
Freud
Tyrer
Paykel

questions.explanation: Hecker subdivided neurasthenia and Freud distinguished between actual neuroses and psychoses. Tyrer introduced the general neurotic syndrome.

questions.question_text: Regarding the classification of neurotic, stress-related and somatoform disorders in ICD-10, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Although the term 'neurotic disorders' has been retained, the concept of neurosis has not been used as a major principle of classification
For the diagnosis of acute stress reaction, the symptoms should occur within 1 hour of exposure to the stressor and disappear within 2–3 days
For the diagnosis of adjustment disorders, the symptoms should occur within 1 month of exposure to a psychological stressor
Post-traumatic stress disorder is described as an adjustment disorder classified under F43.2
The category 'Reaction to severe stress and adjustment disorders' differs from others in that it includes symptoms and causative influences

correct_answer.text: Post-traumatic stress disorder is described as an adjustment disorder classified under F43.2

correct_answers.text: Post-traumatic stress disorder is described as an adjustment disorder classified under F43.2

questions.explanation: Post-traumatic stress disorder is classified under F43, which deals with severe stress and adjustment disorders; under this, PTSD is classified separately as F43.1 and adjustment disorder as F43.2.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), except:

options.text: It arises within 6 months of exposure to the traumatic event
Autonomic disturbances are present
About 50% of people exposed to a potentially traumatic event develop the condition
Female gender is a vulnerability factor
Viewing the dead body of a relative after a disaster is predictive of lower PTSD

correct_answer.text: About 50% of people exposed to a potentially traumatic event develop the condition

correct_answers.text: About 50% of people exposed to a potentially traumatic event develop the condition

questions.explanation: About 25% of people exposed to a potentially traumatic event develop post-traumatic stress disorder.

questions.question_text: The DSM-IV diagnosis of acute stress reaction requires all of the following symptoms, except:

options.text: A sense of numbing or detachment
Increased awareness of surroundings
Derealization
Depersonalization
Dissociative amnesia

questions.explanation: The DSM-IV diagnosis of acute stress reaction requires decreased awareness of the surroundings.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of grief?

options.text: In normal grief, the second stage can last up to 6 months
Depressive symptoms are a frequent component of normal grief
Grief can be considered abnormal if the first stage has not occurred by 2 weeks after the death
Grief can be considered abnormal when the symptoms meet the criteria for a depressive disorder
All of the above

questions.explanation: In ICD-10, grief reaction is classified under 'Adjustment disorders', F43.2.

questions.question_text: Regarding phobic anxiety disorders, all of the following conditions are more common in females, except:

options.text: Agoraphobia
Social phobia
Animal phobia
Miscellaneous specific phobias
None of the above

questions.explanation: Social phobias are equal in both sexes.

questions.question_text: In all types of phobias, high rates of comorbidity are found with:

options.text: Depression
Alcohol abuse
Drug abuse
Obsessive compulsive disorder
All of the above

questions.explanation: Anxiety symptoms are not secondary to other symptoms such as delusions or obsessional thoughts.

questions.question_text: All of the following are thought to be aetiologically linked to phobic anxiety disorders, except:

options.text: Fear of castration in Freud's psychoanalytic theory
Pavlovian classical conditioning
Operant conditioning
Seligman's preparedness theory
Chromosome 18

questions.explanation: Familial aggregation and a three-fold elevated risk of social phobia in relatives have been identified, but no specific chromosomes have been identified.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true of agoraphobia, except:

options.text: The term was first used by Westphal
ICD-10 describes panic disorder as a frequent feature of both present and past episodes
According to DSM-IV, cases with more than 4 panic attacks within 4 weeks are classified as panic disorder with secondary agoraphobic symptoms
Usually onset is in childhood
80% of agoraphobics are never symptom free after 5 years of follow-up

questions.explanation: Most cases begin in the early or mid-20s, and there is a further period of high onset in the mid-30s. Simple phobias begin in childhood and social phobias in the late teens or early 20s.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of panic disorder?

options.text: It requires several attacks within 1 month for diagnosis in ICD-10
Onset is rare after the age of 40
It is twice as common in females
Mitral valve prolapse occurs in 40% of cases
All of the above

questions.explanation: Panic disorder requires unpredictable attacks of severe anxiety lasting usually for a few minutes only.

questions.question_text: Early-onset generalized anxiety disorder is more likely to be associated with all of the following, except:

options.text: Female gender
History of childhood fears
Marital or sexual disturbance
Stressful life events
None of the above

questions.explanation: Stressful life events are more associated with late-onset generalized anxiety disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of obsessive compulsive disorder?

options.text: It is very common in children
It is more common in females
Patients perform well on tests of shifting set
It is frequent in families of probands with Tourettes syndrome, regardless of whether the proband has OCD
It has a good prognosis in males with early onset

correct_answer.text: It is frequent in families of probands with Tourettes syndrome, regardless of whether the proband has OCD

correct_answers.text: It is frequent in families of probands with Tourettes syndrome, regardless of whether the proband has OCD

questions.explanation: Obsessive compulsive disorder is rare in children, there is an equal sex ratio, patients perform poorly on shifting set, and the prognosis in males with early onset is poor.

questions.question_text: All of the following are favourable prognostic factors in obsessive compulsive disorder, except:

options.text: Predominance of phobic ruminative ideas
Absence of compulsions
No childhood symptoms
Symptoms involving the need for symmetry and exactness
Absence of family history of OCD

correct_answer.text: Symptoms involving the need for symmetry and exactness

correct_answers.text: Symptoms involving the need for symmetry and exactness

questions.explanation: Favourable prognostic factors in obsessive compulsive disorder also include short duration of symptoms, whereas males with early onset, need for symmetry and exactness, the presence of hopelessness, hallucinations or delusions, and family history of OCD are associated with poor prognosis.

questions.question_text: Common themes shared by dissociative or conversion disorders include a partial or complete loss of:

options.text: The normal integration between memories of the past
Awareness of identity
Awareness of immediate sensations
Control of bodily movements
All of the above

questions.explanation: Dissociative or conversion disorders are associated with traumatic events, insoluble problems or disturbed relationships.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true of dissociative disorders, except:

options.text: They tend to remit after a few weeks or months, when associated with a traumatic life event
More chronic disorders are associated with symptoms of paralysis and anaesthesias
More chronic disorders are associated with insoluble problems or interpersonal difficulties
Patients present with symptoms representing their concept of how a physical illness would be manifest
They include malingering

questions.explanation: Malingering is feigning illness with an obvious motivation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of dissociative amnesia?

options.text: It is more common in elderly people
It includes memory impairment caused by fatigue
It rarely lasts more than 2 days
The patient usually recovers partially
Recurrence is common

correct_answer.text: It rarely lasts more than 2 days

correct_answers.text: It rarely lasts more than 2 days

questions.explanation: Dissociative amnesia is more common in young adults and is rare in elderly people; memory loss caused by organic states and fatigue is excluded; recovery is complete and recurrence is unusual.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not characteristic of dissociative fugue?

options.text: It may include a purposeful journey away from home
A new identity may be assumed
Self-care and social interaction are impaired
It lasts for hours to days
Recovery is abrupt and complete

correct_answer.text: Self-care and social interaction are impaired

correct_answers.text: Self-care and social interaction are impaired

questions.explanation: Dissociative fugue is precipitated by severe stress; it is characterized by amnesia for the period of stress, though self-care and social relationships are preserved.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a principal feature of Ganser syndrome?

options.text: Approximate answers
Clouding of consciousness
Somatic conversion
Hallucinations
Subsequent amnesia

questions.explanation: Pseudohallucinations are a principal feature of Ganser syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of multiple personality disorder?

options.text: It is not included in ICD-10
Two or more personalities are evident at any time
The dominant personality has access to memories of the other
It includes Couvade's syndrome, which usually occurs in pregnant women
It is viewed in psychoanalysis as a result of childhood trauma beginning before the age of 5

correct_answer.text: It is viewed in psychoanalysis as a result of childhood trauma beginning before the age of 5

correct_answers.text: It is viewed in psychoanalysis as a result of childhood trauma beginning before the age of 5

questions.explanation: Only one personality is evident at a time and one personality does not have access to memories of the other. Couvade's syndrome occurs in men whose partners are pregnant; symptoms include morning sickness, abdominal pain and anxiety.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of somatization disorder?

options.text: It usually begins after the age of 30
It was first described by Briquet
It is four times more common in women than men
It occurs commonly with alexithymia
It is characterized by multiple recurrent somatic complaints for at least 1 year

questions.explanation: Somatization disorder is characterized in ICD-10 by 2 years of symptoms. It begins before the age of 30. It was described by the St Louis group and named after Briquet, who wrote a monograph on hysteria.

questions.question_text: Body dysmorphic disorder:

options.text: Is separately classified in DSM-IV
Is a subgroup of hypochondriasis in ICD-10
Was first described as dymorphophobia by Morselli
May involve complaints about any part of the body
All of the above

questions.explanation: The separate validity of body dysmorphic disorder has not yet been established and there are overlaps with delusional disorder, hypochondriasis and obsessive compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: ICD-10 categories of personality disorder include all of the following, except:

options.text: Schizotypal
Paranoid
Dissocial
Anancastic
Dependent

questions.explanation: Schizotypal personality disorder is included in DSM-IV.

questions.question_text: Which of the following subtypes of personality disorder is more common in men?

options.text: Borderline
Antisocial
Histrionic
Dependent
All of the above

questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is described in DSM-IV. Features include: callous, transient relationships; irresponsible, impulsive and irritable behaviour; lack of guilt and remorse; and failure to accept responsibility.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true of antisocial personality disorder?

options.text: It is twice as common in males as in females
It is twice as prevalent in inner cities as in rural areas
Spontaneous remission may occur in middle age
It is characterized by excess mortality
Antisocial behaviours do not develop after the age of 18

correct_answer.text: It is twice as common in males as in females

correct_answers.text: It is twice as common in males as in females

questions.explanation: The male:female sex ratio in antisocial personality disorder is 7:1.

questions.question_text: Regarding psychodynamic theories of aetiology of personality disorders, all of the following are correctly paired, except:

options.text: Paranoid personality–Projection of castration anxiety
Histrionic personality–Difficulties at the oedipal stage
Dependent personality–Fixation at the oral stage
Obsessive personality/compulsive personality–Difficulties at the anal stage
Borderline personality–Enduring rage and self-hatred caused by sustained neglect and early traumatic experiences

questions.explanation: One of the characteristics of paranoid personality is projection of homosexual impulses.

questions.question_text: All of the following are requirements for a diagnosis of anorexia nervosa, except:

options.text: Body weight below 20% of the normal or expected weight for the age and height
Self-induced weight loss
Body image distortion
Endocrine disorder of the hypothalamo–pituitary–gonadal axis
Amenorrhoea in women and loss of sexual interest and potency in men

correct_answer.text: Body weight below 20% of the normal or expected weight for the age and height

correct_answers.text: Body weight below 20% of the normal or expected weight for the age and height

questions.explanation: Body weight below 15% is needed for a diagnosis of anorexia nervosa.

questions.question_text: The physical signs and complications of anorexia include all of the following, except:

options.text: Bradycardia
Peripheral oedema
Hypothermia
Mitral valve stenosis
An increase in ventricular:brain ratio on neuroimaging

questions.explanation: Mitral valve prolapse occurs in anorexia.

questions.question_text: All of the following are common blood abnormalities in anorexia, except:

options.text: Hyperkalaemia
Hypophosphataemia
Hypercholesterolaemia
Hypercarotenaemia
Hypomagnaesemia

questions.explanation: Hypokalaemia is a common blood abnormality in anorexia.

questions.question_text: Higher prevalence of anorexia is found in all of the following, except:

options.text: Females
Higher socioeconomic class
Patients whose parents have a low level of education
Western Caucasians
Ballet or modelling schools

correct_answer.text: Patients whose parents have a low level of education

correct_answers.text: Patients whose parents have a low level of education

questions.explanation: Higher prevalence of anorexia is found in patients whose parents have a higher level of education.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of bulimia nervosa?

options.text: It shares the same specific psychopathology of fear of fatness as anorexia nervosa
It involves recurrent episodes of over-eating at least twice a week for a period of 3 months
It is associated with craving for food
Metabolic acidosis occurs in laxative abuse
All of the above

questions.explanation: High prevalence of depression, self-mutilation, attempted suicide, substance abuse and low self-esteem are seen in bulimia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: The female:male ratio in bulimia is the same as that in anorexia
Average age of onset is slightly lower in bulimia than anorexia
Social class distribution is slightly more even in bulimia than anorexia
Patients with bulimia can be of normal weight, slightly underweight or overweight
In bulimia, menstrual abnormalities occur in more than 50% of patients

correct_answer.text: Average age of onset is slightly lower in bulimia than anorexia

correct_answers.text: Average age of onset is slightly lower in bulimia than anorexia

questions.explanation: Average age of onset is higher in bulimia than anorexia.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about Diogenes syndrome are true, except:

options.text: It occurs in elderly people
It is characterized by extreme hoarding of rubbish
Alcohol or frontal lobe dysfunction may play a part
Its most common cause is schizophrenia
It is associated with poor prognosis

correct_answer.text: Its most common cause is schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: Its most common cause is schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Diogenes syndrome is mostly unaccompanied by any psychiatric disorder.

questions.question_text: Regarding cross-cultural psychiatry, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Catatonic schizophrenia is more common in developing countries
Hysteria is more common in developing countries
Many cultures do not have the language to express the same feeling of depression as described in the West
Schizophrenia as defined by operational research criteria is not higher in people of Afro-Caribbean origin living in the UK compared with British White people and Asians
Immigrant groups have a higher rate of suicide by burning, with a nine-fold excess among Indian women

correct_answer.text: Schizophrenia as defined by operational research criteria is not higher in people of Afro-Caribbean origin living in the UK compared with British White people and Asians

correct_answers.text: Schizophrenia as defined by operational research criteria is not higher in people of Afro-Caribbean origin living in the UK compared with British White people and Asians

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia as defined by operational research criteria is higher in people of Afro-Caribbean origin living in the UK compared with British White people and Asians.
